And China as a market is coming under pressure for a large part of the OEMs since global OEMs have traditionally have a large part of their revenues coming from that market, right? So that doesn't go away.

items.statement: Investing in digital, AI, engineering technologies across verticals targeting efficiency and quality in product engineering
items.quote: We continue to invest strongly in digital, AI, engineering technologies across the verticals targeting efficiency and quality in product engineering and novel applications of GenAI combined with domain and design expertise to solve complex business, product and engineering problems.

items.statement: Engaging with semiconductor fab companies in India (including Tata Electronics) for design and Industry 4.0 offerings; early stages

items.statement: Large media deal won against 12-15 global competitors; automotive consolidation deals also highly competitive
items.quote: in case of some large consolidation deals, whether there's immense competition 12, 15 companies bidding for a deal and so on. Yes, there will be some amount of margin pressures.

items.statement: No rebadging involved in USD100 million media consolidation deal; deal structured for best-cost country delivery

items.quote: One is approval to explore divesting and monetizing stakes of Symphony India into Climate Technologies, Australia and IMPCO, Mexico.

items.statement: GSK China to sell technology know-how and nine IPRs to IMPCO Mexico for USD 5.1 million (~₹43.5 crores)
items.quote: Second outcome is to sell the technology know -how and nine IPRs by GSK China to IMPCO Mexico for about USD 5.1 million i.e. close to ₹ 43 crores.

items.statement: Climate Technologies Australia trailing 12M to Dec 2024: revenue ₹167 crores, negative EBITDA ₹21 crores, capital employed ₹351 crores

items.statement: IMPCO Mexico trailing 12M to Dec 2024: revenue ₹187 crores, EBITDA ₹24 crores, capital employed ₹86 crores (seasonal low)
items.quote: Coming to IMPCO Mexico, trailing 12 months up to 31st December '24, top line was ₹187 crores, EBITDA was ₹24 crores, and its capital employed was ₹86 crores.

items.statement: Combined overseas subsidiaries ROCE (EBITDA/Capital Employed) only 1%; core India+China ROCE ~583% on ₹46 crores capital employed

items.statement: No public ROCE or revenue targets for FY26; internal targets exist but not disclosed per IR policy

items.statement: US market opportunity emerging due to 145% tariff on China vs 26% on India; direct inquiries received in recent weeks
items.quote: Currently as we speak, the duty on China is about 145%, while on India, it is 26%. Assuming over a period of time, duty from China rationalizes, we still have a decent arbitrage even in that respect as Chinese players don't have that kind of profit margin.

items.statement: US buyers are large retailers (Home Depot, Lowe's, Walmart) with no loyalty; Chinese suppliers dominated but now face high tariffs
items.quote: these buyers are, like you rightly said, are large retailers like The Home Depot and Lowe's and Walmart. And there, there is no loyalty. Every year, they shop around for a different supplier

items.statement: No manufacturing plant planned in US; will continue exporting from India and China; trading subsidiary model like Brazil if needed
items.quote: No. That wouldn't be necessary because we can continue to export from India.

items.statement: GSK China loan to Symphony India outstanding ₹49.6 crores; ~₹40 crores net proceeds from IPR sale to repay loan, leaving ~₹10 crores

items.statement: Stated payout policy ≥60% of PAT; actual payout >70% last 10 years; buybacks and special dividends used when capital not needed
items.quote: we have a stated payout policy whereby at least 60 % of the PAT is to be distributed and in reality, I think in last 10 years, our payout is more than 70% out of a PAT.

items.statement: IMPCO Mexico to fund IPR purchase (₹43 crores) from internal accruals and working capital squeeze over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: this ₹43 crores of payment , we expect to happen in the next 2 to 3 quarters. So, one out of internal accruals, which is already and expected to be very healthy. And secondly, IMPCO, Mexico has worked out the plan to squeeze its working capital.

items.statement: IPR sale structured to be tax efficient, complying with transfer pricing guidelines; IMPCO Mexico dividend historically not tax efficient
items.quote: end -to-end, this transaction is also quite tax efficient, fully complying with all the regulatory requirements, including transfer pricing guidelines.

items.statement: India growth driven by adjacent categories: table-top cooling, kitchen cooling, storage water heaters (counter-seasonal); rural/semi-urban penetration and digital channels
items.quote: those initiatives include our entry into adjacent product categories like table-top cooling appliances as well as kitchen cooling solutions both are selling around the year and have immense potential to grow profitably. Last year, we have launched innovative storage water heaters, which is counter seasonal.

items.statement: Climate Technologies Australia expanded into air conditioning, reverse cycle, heating, fans — now addressing AUD 6-7 billion market vs few hundred million earlier
items.quote: Now that we have ventured into air conditioning and into reverse ducted cycle air conditioning into heating and into fans, C limate Technologies, Australia is playing in a multibillion -dollar market. We're talking about some AU$6 billion - AUD$7 billion market that it is playing in

items.statement: Group CEO Amit Kumar (mid-40s) leads India business; CEO International Rajesh Mishra (~50s) leads global revenue; both driving growth
items.quote: Kumar, who is on the call as well, who is the Group CEO & Director, who is currently focusing more on the India business, and he's demonstrated very good growth, as you have seen in the past, in the last few quarters. And then there is Rajesh Mishra, who is right here with me. He heads the International Business

items.statement: Non-compete terms with buyers of Climate Technologies Australia (which has US subsidiary) unknown; will try to retain US market access
items.quote: That is a little too premature to gauge at this point, Aditya. It all depends on how the negotiation unfolds with potential or prospective buyers.

items.statement: Symphony India exports to IMPCO Mexico and Climate Technologies Australia only 3-4% of ₹1,065 crores standalone revenue; GSK China exports ~20% of ₹86 crores to Climate Technologies
items.quote: Out of this, export to IMPCO, Mexico and Climate Technologies, Australia won't be more than 3 - 4%. I'm saying indicative figure.

items.statement: New owners of Climate Technologies Australia and IMPCO Mexico likely to continue sourcing from Symphony India and GSK China due to product fit and retailer continuity
items.quote: most of the retailers in this market like continuity. So, for that reason also, the new buyer may not want to , also it will be too risky for them to change the product line overnight.

items.statement: Symphony India treasury ~₹600 crores; even if overseas investments written off, no material impact on financial position
items.quote: finally, apart from this currently, Symphony, India is sitting on a treasury of ~ ₹600 crores. So, in the worst scenario, assuming everything else we have to write off, still it doesn't change anything

items.statement: Commercial lines expected to return to double digit growth at industry level in FY2026

items.quote: Combined ratio for Q4 FY2025 was 102.5% as against 102.3% in Q4 FY2024.

items.quote: However, in Q4 FY2025, we have seen a de-growth of 1.9% for the Two-wheeler segment and a de-growth of 4.6% for the Tractor segment. This indicates a softer rural demand.

items.statement: Fire pricing pressure caused industry de-growth of 5.3% in FY2025
items.quote: Within this, the Fire segment registered a de-growth of 1.8% and 5.3% for Q4 FY2025 and FY2025 respectively on account of pricing pressure.

items.statement: Early signs of improved Fire pricing discipline seen in first weeks of April 2025

items.statement: Motor TP price hike sought by industry but not yet implemented

items.quote: key circulars which were introduced in Q4 FY2025, regarding capping the increase in senior citizens Health insurance premium rates to 10% per annum

items.quote: and the introduction of BIMA-ASBA facility for Health insurance policies.

items.statement: Investment assets rose to ₹535.08 billion at March 31, 2025 from ₹515.97 billion at December 31, 2024

items.statement: Investment portfolio duration slightly above 5.3 years, yield to maturity at 7.55%
items.quote: our duration of the book. That still continues to be slightly in excess of 5.3 years. And if you look at the yield to maturity, the yield to maturity of the book also currently stands at about 7.55%.

items.statement: Motor advance premium at ₹37.17 billion as at March 31, 2025 vs ₹36.44 billion at December 31, 2024

items.quote: Full year, this number for Corporate Health is at 97.6% and Retail Indemnity is 67.9%.

This payment is, however, subject to approval of shareholders in the ensuing Annual General Meeting of the Company. The overall dividend for FY2025, including the proposed final dividend is ₹ 12.50 per share. Last year, the overall dividend was ₹ 11.00 per share.

items.statement: Solvency ratio at 2.69x as at March 31, 2025 vs 2.36x at December 31, 2024, well above regulatory minimum of 1.50x
items.quote: Solvency ratio was at 2.69x as at March 31, 2025, as against 2.36x as at December 31, 2024, continued to be higher than the regulatory minimum requirement of 1.50x.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments pose risk to global growth and Indian economy

items.quote: Increasing unique customer visit by 2x on our digital platforms. 37% growth in fresh transactions on our digital platforms. Downloads for our one-stop solution, 'IL TakeCare App', surpassed 14.9 million.

items.quote: Our Preferred Partner Network (PPN) serviced 74.1% of our non-OEM claims in Q4 FY2025, up from 69.6% in Q4 FY2024.

items.quote: We anticipate quarter 4 FY '26 will mark a normalized quarter with operational and profitability metrics returning to their previous levels.

items.quote: This includes ₹ 344 million we spent on IPL associate partnership sponsorship and related digital and advert media spends during the quarter, which was not there in the previous quarter in addition to our regular brand spend.

items.quote: I'm pleased to introduce Rohit Chatter as our Chief Data Officer. Rohit brings over 29 years of experience in driving AI and data innovation at scale.

items.statement: F&O regulation caused immediate volume decline, reduced active clients, muted order activity; viewed as temporary recalibration

items.quote: Finance cost decreased by 3.9% quarter-on-quarter to ₹ 803 million pursuant to a marginal decrease in average cost of borrowings. However, the average quantum of borrowings were higher by 7.3% quarter-on-quarter, primarily for margin requirements at the clearing corporations.

But going forward, always this is the practice, we do some projection based on that, we work out fixed and variable pay. So for coming year also, same system would be followed.

items.statement: ROE expected to trend back to historical levels as business normalizes over next few quarters

items.quote: Our EBITDA performance for this quarter de-grew by 1.4% and our net profit de-grew by 14.4%. The de-growth in EBITDA in spite of the positive momentum and growth in revenue is largely attributable to 3 or 4 important reasons.

items.statement: UK margins dipped due to newer Data & AI capabilities delivered on-site and lower-margin SGS renewals; recovery expected mid-term
items.quote: The business that we are gaining a lot of the NHS business as well as some of the business that we are now delivering in secured government services have been secured at a lower gross margin as compared to the gross margins that Mastek traditionally has been used to.

items.statement: UK revenue grew 17.2% YoY and 9.4% QoQ in Q4; healthcare grew over 100% YoY in FY25 driven by NHS prevention and collections programs
items.quote: Our revenue for U.K. on a year-on-year basis grew more than 17.2%, which is an outstanding performance from a U.K. standpoint. In fact, the numbers also grew by 9.4% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: US revenue grew 16% YoY but declined 8% QoQ in Q4 due to macro uncertainty, public sector budget cuts, insourcing, and right-shifting of orders
items.quote: As far as our North America business is concerned, again, our business for the quarter, while it had a year-on-year growth of around 16%, our Q-o-Q numbers have dropped by 8%.

items.statement: 12-month order backlog grew 1.7% YoY; adding a $15M ACV deal closed in early April brings growth to 7-8% YoY and ~12% QoQ
items.quote: The 12-m onth backlog for year -on-year is 1.7%. Having said that, there's almost a $15 million worth of contract, which based on our cycle has closed in the first week of April, which we haven't counted there–which is $15 million ACV. So, if I add that $15 million, then the 12-month backlog also moves more close to 7% to 8% on an annual basis

items.statement: Renewed all large SGS backlog contracts, securing 2-year runway; now targeting net new growth in SGS with active bids
items.quote: This year, as planned, we have almost renewed all the large backlog of business that we had to renew, which gives us a very st rong healthy runway for the next 2 years and also gives us the momentum to aggressively go out and hunt for much more net new growth business in the coming

items.statement: Investing disproportionately in Data & AI capabilities across geographies; added 50-100 people to Data AI team of 200-250
items.quote: Our investments in Data & AI will continue to be disproportionate to some of the other capability areas as we really go forward into the next year.

items.statement: Data & AI expanding across service lines: ADOPT.AI platform extended from Oracle to Salesforce and Digital; 100+ AI use cases developed
items.quote: The ADOPT.AI platform that we had launched earlier in Q3 for Oracle services has now been extended to all the other service lines, including Salesforce and Digital. So we now have an AI-led sales force implementation as well as an AI-led legacy modernization platform.

items.statement: AI delivering 30-50% efficiency on fixed-bid projects across Oracle, Digital, Salesforce; passing ~30% efficiency to clients
items.quote: We've already seen customers where we are seeing more than 30% efficiency benefits as we are executing, especially the fixed bid projects that we execute across Oracle, Digital and Salesforce using AI and AI-enabled technologies.

items.statement: Added 11 new customers in Q4; targeting 40-50 net new customers annually while reducing tail customers
items.quote: So we've added 11 new customers this quarter. And we continue to see that as a healthy rate of adding like 40-50 customers, while we're also trying to reduce the tail customers that we have

items.statement: US top clients saw project go-lives in March; negotiating MSAs with additional Blue Cross Blue Shield plans for next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: As we speak, we are actually negotiating MSAs with a few Blues. So hopefully, in the next 1 or 2 quarters, we would have added a few more MSAs beyond BCBS in the Blues.

items.statement: SGS renewals were single-sourced avoiding competition; now positioned to compete for competitor-held SGS business
items.quote: The government clearly is renegotiating prices and is looking at cost efficiencies from all vendors, which I think our ability since we closed most of our open book of business today gives us the license to go out and compete against the book of businesses that other competitors have.

items.statement: DSOs improved to 83 days in Q4, meeting fiscal target; cash generation grew >30% YoY
items.quote: In fact, it has come down to 83 days in this quarter, which has been our target that we have set ourselves up for the fiscal. So overall, we see a healthy working capital balance and we feel quite comfortable with the cash g eneration that we have

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents grew to INR 622 crores from INR 473 crores at end of FY24
items.quote: The total cash and cash equivalent that we had in the company has now grown to INR 622 crores as compared to INR 473 crores that we had at the end of last year.

items.statement: Declared final dividend of INR 16, making cumulative dividend 460% for FY25
items.quote: For this year, we have also declar ed a final dividend of INR 16, which makes up a cumulative dividend of 460% for the year

items.statement: Headcount reduced overall but on-site headcount increased, raising costs; leadership restructuring executed with one-time costs in Q4 and Q1
items.quote: a lot of the increase in headcount that has happened in this quarter, is largely on-site resources. And these are pretty high cost on onshore or on-sit e resources that we have hired. And that has led to this increase in cost despite of overall reduction in headcount

items.statement: Data AI team of 200-250 people growing by 50-100 quarterly through reskilling and new hires
items.quote: So our current Data AI team, is around 200, 250-plus people, but it is growing as we speak, growing quarter-on-quarter. So we're adding another 50-100 people.

items.statement: Oracle business grew >50% YoY in US driven by healthcare, manufacturing, utilities; expanding to higher education globally
items.quote: Our Oracle business, in fact, grew more than 50% in this year as compared to the previous year and we continue to see a very strong momentum in the Oracle business.

items.statement: AMEA EBITDA improved significantly QoQ; restructuring completed, focus on profitable healthcare growth across Oracle, Salesforce, Data & AI
items.quote: Our EBITDA numbers for the geography have improved significantly quarter-over-quarter and we continue to focus on driving healthy profitable growth in the region.

items.statement: Near-term macro uncertainty in US and UK (NHS merger) may cause deal delays; navigating with positivity and caution
items.quote: The near-term uncertainties in the market continue as we look at and get into the next year from an overall sentiment point of view. We are driving with a lot of positivity as well as caution to make sure that we understand the changes well and we navigate the business well.

items.statement: NHS England merger into Department of Health is 2+ year process; technology investment in prevention and collections programs continues
items.quote: The merger of NHS England into Department of Health that got announced earlier in the quarter, currently, this process is going to be a steady long-term process. It will take at least 2 years for the government to really integrate and put the 2 departments together.

items.statement: SGS contracts renewed at lower gross margins but avoided commercial competition; internal efficiency drives underway to restore margins
items.quote: On the secured government services side, the large contracts that we have renewed now, which gave us a more healthy 2-year runway for these businesses have been renewed at a lower gross margin rate. However, we've been able to avoid any commercial competition there.

items.statement: Operational efficiency program targets 15-20% efficiency from AI adoption in fixed-bid delivery; also simplifying org structure and resourcing pyramids
items.quote: Third is adoption of AI in all of our internal delivery programs, especially the ones which are fixed bid delivery programs. And we are looking forward to anywhere between a 15% to 20% efficiency drive just because of AI adoption in our business.

items.statement: Not investing in NetSuite (too small for SMB); evaluating Cerner partnership pending Oracle opening it for partners
items.quote: We are not investing in NetSuite. NetSuite is more for the SMB market. Cerner, we are evaluating closely whether we want to invest in Cerner or not. But it's a degree that we are working closely with Oracle. As soon as they open up Cerner for partners, we would want to invest.

items.statement: UK and Europe remain core growth markets; US reset underway with focus on Data & AI, Oracle, Salesforce, Digital integration
items.quote: Our current view is our growth in our core business and core markets, which is our U.K. and Europe geographies will continue to be extremely healthy. As I mentioned earlier, we are almost firing all cylinders in our U.K. market.

items.statement: Rebalancing on-site/offshore mix and resourcing pyramids to align with customer cost efficiency demands
items.quote: Last and not the least is reorganizing our business to deliver the kind of growth that we have set in U.K. So reorganizing, relooking at our resourcing our pyramids, our on-site offshore mix between our resources to make sure that the cost efficiency demand that we have for our customers, we are organizing our internal org structure to align to those kinds of demand.

items.statement: Industry grew 5.1% CAGR in hectares covered from FY21 to FY24 per PDMC data
items.quote: If we compare F '21 to F'24, we do see a bounce back of the industry and a growth of 5.1% compounded annual growth rate in lakh hectares covered as per the official site of the PDMC.

items.statement: Industry slightly degrew or was nearly flat in FY25 versus FY24
items.quote: In what we estimate as an industry that has had a slight degrowth or is nearly flat versus FY'24, your Company has registered a growth of around 4%.

items.statement: Company registered 4% revenue growth in FY25 with total income of Rs 275.1 crore vs Rs 265.5 crore in FY24
items.quote: your Company has registered a growth of around 4%, with Rs. 275.1 crore as our total Income versus Income in F '24 of Rs. 265.5 crores.

items.statement: PBT improved to Rs 10.71 crore in FY25 from Rs 2.43 crore in FY24
items.quote: Also, the company has improved its bottomline, delivering a PBT of Rs. 10.71 crores for F'25 versus a PBT of Rs. 2.43 crores in F'24.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue grew 32% to Rs 97.43 crore, highest ever Q4 revenue; PBT Rs 9.43 crore vs Rs 2.1 crore in Q4 FY24
items.quote: For the fourth quarter of F'25, your company registered a revenue of Rs. 97.43 crores versus Rs. 73.78 crores in F'24. This is a growth of 32%, which is in fact the highest ever Q4 revenue the company has registered so far.

items.statement: Material cost saving of 2.6% from soft raw material prices and strategic sourcing; additional 4.8% from mix impact
items.quote: During the year, raw material prices were soft to stable. And this, along with other strategic sourcing initiatives that we have carried out, have together enabled your company to deliver a material cost saving of 2.6% versus FY'24.

items.statement: Non-subsidy business contribution reached 33.4% in FY25 from 3% in FY20
items.quote: In fact, as a consequence of this, you will be happy to note that we have reached a 33.4% contribution of the non -subsidy business, which was a mere 3% contribution to the total business in FY'20.

items.statement: Unrecognized work order pipeline of Rs 76 crore for irrigation projects in non-subsidy business
items.quote: Specifically, speaking about the non -subsidy business, in the projects area, we have an unrecognized work order pipeline of Rs. 76 crore for irrigation projects.

items.statement: Debtors higher as of March 31, 2025 due to revenue skew to last four months (over 45% of annual revenue) and longer collection cycles in opportunity states
items.quote: As a result, as of 31st March 2025, the debtors were higher versus the previous years. But this, of course, is a normal phenomenon in any year where we have a significant skew towards the last four months of the year.

items.statement: Company mitigated working capital impact through efficient inventory and payables management
items.quote: But overall, your company has mitigated to a great extent the impact on working ca pital through the efficient management of its inventory as well as its payables.

items.statement: Evaluating new satellite unit location to service growing northern markets (UP, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh); currently have units in Coimbatore and Baroda
items.quote: Now, do we want to relook at this in light of the growing sales opportunities in these states? The answer is yes and we are currently in the process of figuring out where exactly to locate that satellite.

items.statement: Ami Goda appointed Non-Independent Director; she is CFO of Mahindra Farm Equipment Sector with GE background
items.quote: So she is the Head of Finance of the Farm Equipment Sector, which is in Mahindra & Mahindra. That sector, which looks after our mechanization business, our farm machinery business, our Agri business as well as some other businesses that roll into the Farm Equipment Sector. And she is the CFO of that business.

items.statement: PM pushing for 1 crore hectares (10 million) coverage in next 5 years (2 million hectares/year) vs estimated 1.1 million hectares in FY25
items.quote: The first data point is something that I've shared before and something that is often repeated by the honorable Prime Minister who is pushing for 1 crore hectares or 10 million hectares to be covered in the next five years. And this translates to 2 million hectares a year versus what we estimate to be a 1.1 million hectares of micro irrigation actually done in FY'25.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh targeting 3 lakh hectares/year for next 4 years vs 1.2 lakh hectares in FY25
items.quote: certain states like AP, which have real ly taken the objective of micro irrigation very seriously and have requested assistance to cover 3,00,000 hectares a year over the next four years . As reference, FY '25 AP coverage was 1.2 lakh hectares.

items.statement: Multiple ministries working on scheme convergence; groundwater efficiency via Atal Bhujal Yojana, pressurized piping in major irrigation projects, command area modernization approved as sub-scheme under Krishi Sinchayi Yojana with Rs 1,600
items.quote: In fact, in a recent cabinet meeting, this has been approved as a sub-scheme under Krishi Sinchayi Yojana with a budget of Rs. 1600 crores. The effect of this, of course, will be realized in improving the area and the micro irrigation in the future.

items.statement: Exploring export markets as part of non-subsidy business growth strategy
items.quote: Besides this, of course, in the non -subsidy area, we are also exploring exports markets.

items.statement: Subsidy-driven market ebbs and flows; geopolitical events may impact raw material price outlook
items.quote: Right now, we are seeing good things . But we all do know that the subsidy-driven market, it ebbs and flows.

items.statement: Micro irrigation potential estimated at 72 million hectares (14-15% covered so far at 9.7 million hectares)
items.quote: My impression is this is still only about 14% to 15% of the total identified current potential for micro irrigation in India and that potential is estimated at 72 million hectares.

items.statement: Non-subsidy business includes farmers buying without subsidy (ISI and thin wall), institutions, and exports
items.quote: So in the non-subsidy, you do have farmer revenue, which comes from selling micro irrigation without the benefit of subsidy. But we also have segments which are not farmers, which are like institutions . So that actually for us is a very interesting idea and is something that we're looking at to grow. Exports is also something that we would improve in our non-subsidy

items.statement: Non-subsidy margins variable; some close to subsidy segment, some lower
items.quote: And some of them would be relatively close to our subsidy segment, but some of them would be less than the subsidy segment.

items.statement: Other expenses increased due to irrigation projects growth; projects have lower material cost but higher onsite installation, civil work, labor costs
items.quote: So while that has helped our topline and revenue growth, it has a certain cost structure. And like I was explaining to Aditya, that cost structure helps us reduce our material costs because they consume less materials when we run these irrigation projects . But these irrigation projects have other expenses in t erms of onsite installation, civil work, labor etc.

items.statement: Demand generation through farm demonstrations, Mahindra dealer network synergy, institutional segments, product innovations (gravity feed, QPC Lite thin wall)
items.quote: We show farmers the benefits of micro -irrigation in terms of productivity, in terms of electricity saving, in terms of labor saving and this is really done by people on the ground in the last m ile in partnership with our channels. We also take support from the Mahindra & Mahindra team, which has an extensive dealer network, as you know, for tractors

items.statement: Expects to reach Rs. 200 crore revenue from toys business in FY26
items.quote: We should be doing that. I do not comment on specific numbers, but we should be doing that.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin expected at 20-22%
items.quote: Yes, the blended would be about 20% to 22%, yes.

items.statement: Phase 2 toys expansion planned at Rs. 100 crore, break ground in H2 FY26
items.quote: The total planned investment for Phase 2 is about Rs. 100 crore. We also intend to benefit from the upcoming production linked incentive scheme and the toy sector policies announced in the Union Budget, which are expected to provide capital subsidies and rebates.

items.statement: Phase 2 plant expected to take 6-10 months to commission after break ground
items.quote: We plan to invest about Rs. 100 crore and we plan to do this by the second-half of FY '26. And I think it should be taking about anywhere from 6 to 10 months to put the plant in place.

items.statement: Phase 1 toys capacity at Rs. 14-15 crore per month, currently running at Rs. 9-10 crore per month
items.quote: We have a capacity of doing about Rs. 14 crore to Rs. 15 crore a month in toys.

items.statement: Secured strategic order from Escorts for blow molded components for construction and agricultural verticals
items.quote: We have recently secured a strategic order from Escorts for blow molded components supporting their construction and agricultural verticals. We expect these new partnerships to begin contributing meaningfully to revenues from FY '26 onwards.

items.statement: Manufacturing roto and blow molded components for Vestas and Indocool
items.quote: Notably, we are now manufacturing roto and blow molded components for prominent clients such as Vestas and Indocool.

items.statement: Toy segment grew 40% QoQ in Q4 FY25, strong momentum and increasing market share
items.quote: Our toy segment continues to be a key growth engine. In Q4 of FY ‘25, the toys business grew by approximately 40% on quarter-to-quarter basis, u nderscoring strong momentum and increasing market share

items.statement: Automotive components division declined 25% QoQ in Q4 FY25 aligned with CV sector trends
items.quote: Starting with the automotive components division, which primarily serves the commercial vehicle segment, witnessed a sequential decline of around 25% in quarter four. This underperformance is aligned with the broader market trends within the CV sector.

items.statement: CV business projection for FY26 looks good and much better than FY25
items.quote: In fact, the coming year FY '26 the projection that we have got, even from a CV business perspective, looks good and much better than what we did in FY '25.

items.statement: India has cost advantage with tariffs on Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Thailand at 32-46% vs India's 10%
items.quote: It is worth noting that India enjoys a clear cost advantage relative to regional competitors with tariffs wars with Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia and Thailand ranging between 32% and 46%.

items.statement: US imposed 145% tariff on Chinese toys vs 10% on India, potential to reduce to 5-6% via bilateral talks
items.quote: The US has recently imposed a steep 145% tariff on toys being imported from China, compared to India's base rate of 10%, presenting a golden opportunity for Indian manufacturers to expand their footprint in the global toy market.

items.statement: Current toy supply 95% domestic, Phase 2 focused on export market
items.quote: The demand right now, 95% of our current supply is to the domestic market.

items.statement: Strong relationships with Amazon, Hamleys, Blinkit, Lifelong; 85 distributors in India
items.quote: We have built strong relationships with major partners, including Amazon, Hamleys, Blinkit and Lifelong, and we are confident of reaching peak capacity utilization soon.

items.statement: In talks with several large US toy companies for JV, white labeling or OEM manufacturing
items.quote: We are in talks with several large toy companies from the US to either do a joint venture or to do white labeling or OEM manufacturing to cater to their range of products.

items.statement: Toy sales mix: 30-35% contract manufacturing, 65-70% own brands
items.quote: No, no, it's I would say about 30%, 35% is contract manufacturing and the remaining is our own brands.

items.statement: Phase 2 to add battery operated ride-ons and role play products via injection molding
items.quote: We are preparing to launch Phase 2 with phase fully focused on injection molded toys, including battery operated ride ons and role play products.

items.statement: BIS certification mandatory for toys in India, product-specific not plant-specific
items.quote: So BIS is now mandatory. It's a legal prerequisite to sell toys in India. And it does not depend on where the company is, even if there are companies outside India they need to have the BIS certification in India.

items.statement: Automotive receivables 90 days, toys receivables 60 days
items.quote: For our automotive business, it's usually 90 days and for the toys business it's about 60 days.

items.statement: Management stressed on not taking substantial debt, reduced debt in past quarters, funding Phase 2 largely via equity
items.quote: we will not be kind of getting into a situation where we have a substantial amount of debt sitting on our balance sheet. T his is something that the management is also stressed upon. And if you see, in the past few quarters also we have reduced our debt quite a bit

items.statement: Preferential allotment underway, closing shortly
items.quote: Yes, yes, that is under way as of now and we would be closing this shortly.

items.statement: Subsidiary MRH Technologies (51% owned) signed exclusive 10-year licensing agreement with MANN+HUMMEL for air purifiers in India
items.quote: Our subsidiary, MRH Technologies Private Limited, has signed an exclusive 10 year licensing agreement with MANN+HUMMEL, a global leader in the filtration technology for manufacturing and distribution of air purifiers in India.

items.statement: India toy exports grew from $40M in FY15 to $152M in FY24; imports from China fell from $235M in FY20 to $41M in FY24
items.quote: India's toys exports have grown steadily from $40 million in FY ‘ 15 to an estimated $152 million in the FY ‘ 24. Meanw hile, toy imports from China have declined significantly from $235 million in FY ‘20 to risk $41 million in FY

items.statement: US tariff advantage may last only 90 days until Trump decides; tariff situation fluid
items.quote: In fact, like I mentioned, it's a golden opportunity for the toy manufacturers as of now, at lea st for the next 90 days to show till the time Trump decides

items.statement: Toy business shifted from institutional to retail oriented products, reducing seasonality
items.quote: See, earlier, our business was seasonal because we were doing more of institutional oriented product s which were more cater ed to schools and daycares and creche and all. Now the growth that we are getting is not from the institutional oriented product, it is more from the retail oriented products

items.statement: Air purifier trials at IIT Delhi showed over 80% PM reduction; pilot at GD Goenka School successful; commercial launch planned in current year
items.quote: Results showed over 80% reduction in PM levels in both indoor and outdoor settings. Additionally, we successfully completed a pilot deployment at GD Goenka Public School, achieving significant AQI reduction, which demonstrates the commercial viability and impact of our filtration solutions.

items.statement: Full-year FY2025 NIM of 4.32% is the representative margin to focus on
items.quote: I think the margin number to focus on in our mind is really the 4.3% for the full year. That would be a more representative number.

items.statement: Q4 FY2025 NIM expanded to 4.41% from 4.25% in Q3 FY2025
items.quote: The net interest margin was 4.41% in this quarter compared to 4.25% in the previous quarter and 4.40% in Q4 of last year.

items.statement: Day count convention benefit reversed in Q4 FY2025 boosting NIM
items.quote: I think probably the largest component driving up the yield was what we had spoken of in, I think, Q2 and Q3 last year, which is the benefit of the day count, which brought down the yield in Q2 vis -a-vis Q1.

items.statement: Higher rate cuts expected will impact margins due to lag in deposit repricing
items.quote: Indeed, the expectations of the rate cut have gone up compared to where they were, say, a couple of months ago and a higher level of rate-cut is now expected. At the same time, as we spoke earlier, the deposit rates have also started falling. So, we will have to see as we go along how we manage through this. But there would be an impact on margins definitely.

items.statement: Unsecured retail loan growth has bottomed out and may improve from here
items.quote: On the unsecured side, probably the growth has bottomed-out. And we may see some improved growth from here is what we feel.

items.statement: Vehicle loan slowdown driven by underlying demand and marginal pricing pressure
items.quote: I think it's more the underlying demand and maybe at the margin a little bit on the pricing side, nothing on asset quality per se.

items.statement: Net NPA ratio improved to 0.39% in March 2025 from 0.42% in December 2024
items.quote: The net NPA ratio was 0.39% at March 31, 2025 compared to 0.42% at December 31, 2024 and 0.42% at March 31, 2024.

items.statement: Gross NPA additions declined to Rs 51.42 bn in Q4 FY2025 from Rs 60.85 bn in Q3 FY2025
items.quote: The gross NPA additions were 51.42 billion Rupees in the current quarter compared to 60.85 billion Rupees in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Unsecured retail NPL formation broadly stabilised but not yet coming down meaningfully
items.quote: unsecured, I think that generally the NPL formation has broadly stabilised. We would hope for it to come down, but let us wait for that to happen. Maybe it will take another couple of quarters

items.statement: Contingency provisions of Rs 131 bn maintained at 1% of total advances
items.quote: In addition, the Bank continues to hold contingency provisions of 131.00 billion Rupees or about 1.0% of total advances at March 31, 2025.

items.statement: Domestic loan portfolio grew 13.9% YoY and 2.2% QoQ to March 31, 2025
items.quote: The domestic loan portfolio grew by 13.9% year-on-year and 2.2% sequentially at March 31, 2025.

items.statement: Business banking portfolio grew 33.7% YoY and 6.2% QoQ
items.quote: The business banking portfolio grew by 33.7% year -on-year and 6.2% sequentially.

items.statement: Retail loan portfolio grew 8.9% YoY and 2.0% QoQ
items.quote: The retail loan portfolio grew by 8.9% year-on-year and 2.0% sequentially.

items.statement: Overseas loan portfolio declined 10.2% YoY in USD terms
items.quote: The overseas loan portfolio, in US dollar terms, declined 10.2% year-on-year at March 31, 2025.

items.statement: Cost of deposits increased to 5.00% in Q4 FY2025 from 4.91% in Q3 FY2025
items.quote: The cost of deposits was 5.00% in this quarter compared to 4.91% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Deposit rates have started falling following 50 bps repo rate cut
items.quote: And as the repo rate has fallen by 50 bps, so that will start to see a transmission into deposit rates, which is what has started.

items.statement: Large capable competitors priced meaningfully below in retail creating growth challenges
items.quote: Yes, clearly it is an issue. I think in retail, it's not just about pricing because you really need the distribution scale, processing capacity to back up your pricing. So , I wouldn't say it's just about pricing. But certainly there are very large, capable competitors who are also priced meaningfully below us.

items.statement: Branch count increased by 241 in Q4 FY2025 and 460 in FY2025 to 6,983 branches
items.quote: Our branch count has increased by 241 in Q4 and 460 in FY2025. We had 6,983 branches as of March 31, 202 5.

items.statement: Technology expenses were 10.7% of operating expenses in FY2025
items.quote: The technology expenses were about 10.7% of our operating expenses in FY2025.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of Rs 11 per share for FY2025
items.quote: The Board has recommended a dividend of 11 Rupees per share for FY2025, subject to requisite approvals.

items.statement: CET-1 ratio at 15.94% and total CAR at 16.55% after proposed dividend
items.quote: The capital position of the Bank continued to be strong with a CET-1 ratio of 15.94% and total capital adequacy ratio of 16.55% at March 31, 2025, after reckoning the impact of proposed dividend.

items.statement: Capital levels not out of line with peers; focus on maintaining strategic capital buffer
items.quote: I think that there is a certain expectation among stakeholders, market etc. of the level of capital that a large private sector bank should be maintaining. And I think our capital levels are not out of line with most of our peers in that context.

items.statement: Average CASA deposits grew 10.0% YoY and 0.5% QoQ
items.quote: During the quarter, average deposits grew by 11.4% year-on-year and 1.9% sequentially and a verage current and savings account deposits grew by 10.0% year-on-year and 0.5% sequentially.

items.statement: CASA pressure likely behind given monetary easing and improved liquidity
items.quote: I said logically that should be so given the monetary easing, the improvement in system liquidity and to the extent that it was a factor, the sort of some calm in capital markets, but it's something we will have to see as we go ahead.

items.statement: Global trade issues and economic outlook are key risks to monitor
items.quote: Of course, as we go into the year, I think what happens to the overall economy globally and in India and this whole trade relat ed issues is something we will have to watch out for.

items.statement: Profit before tax excluding treasury grew 13.2% YoY to Rs 165.34 bn in Q4 FY2025
items.quote: The profit before tax excluding treasury grew by 13.2% year-on-year to 165.34 billion Rupees in this quarter and by 11.4% year-on-year to 607.13 billion Rupees in FY2025.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT grew 15.7% YoY to Rs 135.02 bn in Q4 FY2025
items.quote: The consolidated profit after tax grew by 15.7% year-on-year to 135.02 billion Rupees in this quarter and by 15.3% year-on-year to 510.29 billion Rupees in FY2025.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance 2% to 5% in constant currency; EBIT margin guidance 18% to 19%
items.quote: With respect to our guidance, as mentioned in our Investor Release , our guidance for FY26 is as follows. The revenue growth guidance for the full year is 2% to 5% in constant currency. EBIT margin guidance is at 18 % to 19%.

items.statement: Q4 net-new bookings $3 billion, second highest quarter; FY25 total new booking TCV $9.3 billion
items.quote: We had a very strong quarter. In fact, the second highest after the September 2023 quarter, which was on the back of a mega deal, which all of you know. This quarter, we did $3 billion of net -new booking. At the fiscal year level, the total new booking TCV stands at $9.3 billion.

items.statement: Engineering and R&D Services booking grew 75% in FY25, record high
items.quote: Our Engineering and R&D Services business had a record high booking, which is a 75% growth in FY25.

items.statement: Pipeline near all-time high with healthy conversions in Q4; AI and GenAI integral to almost every deal

items.statement: Integration of multiple businesses into one seamless entity a key non-financial KPI

items.statement: Q4 depreciation level indicative for full next year

items.quote: We made a loss of around INR11 crores, INR12 crores in Chennai, which has hit the bottom line by around INR11 crores. And I think INR10 crores we have capitalized as trial run losses.

items.statement: Thailand EBITDA margin target of 10-11% for FY26
items.quote: I can see definitely next year, the margins would improve to about 10%, 10% to 11%.

items.statement: Bead wire EBITDA 14-15%, black wire EBITDA 8-9%
items.quote: In bead wire, we are able to hit 14%, 15% EBITDA, in black wire, it is 8%, 9%.

items.statement: Freight savings of INR3,000-4,000 per ton from Chennai plant location
items.quote: Generally, there is a INR3,000 to INR4,000 saving on freight because of the location of Chennai plant, which is closer to customer and a little closer to raw material supplier also.

items.statement: Indian tyre industry growth expected at 5-6%
items.quote: Current outlook remains same. There is whatever we are meeting the customers, we are getting an information that tyre will continue to grow at 5%, 6%, not beyond that.

items.quote: We have approvals from MRF, we have approvals from Apollo. We have approval -- this month and we'll get approval from CEAT, 3 major companies and BKT has approved us long back.

items.quote: Quarter 1 order for next financial year is much higher than what we sold to them in quarter 4 of last year. Moving forward, we see clarity that the volumes would increase. Also trial lots to Bridgestone Europe and Bridgestone America are on the way.

items.quote: And major growth this year, at least 7,000 tons of export will increase. Yashovardhan can talk more about that. So we are targeting 7,000 tons additional exports from Indian ports to U.S. and Europe.

items.quote: So it is partly because of larger export volumes where the material takes about 45 days to reach. And then there is a 1-month payment cycle. So the overall debt number you see is because of that, debtors.

items.quote: So, 12,000 tons of black wire, we will now add value to that product and start making wire ropes. That is the thinking.

items.quote: Yes. So we always had 25% tariff and it remains at 25%. But for China, it was around 30%, 32%, which has now become 59% or 57 %.

items.quote: Right now there is no development to be discussed right now. I'm not in a position to say anything confirmatory at this point of time. We continue to look for a partner.

items.quote: We will try to maintain EBITDA margin in the short-term term or long-term actions on improving business in the right direction.

items.statement: Prices should remain where they are and slightly start firming up if China doesn't dump.
items.quote: But if that doesn't happen, I would say prices should only remain where they are and slightly start firming up.

items.statement: Domestic agrochemical demand is positive with normal rainfall forecast for 2025 monsoon.
items.quote: Domestic agrochemical demand is positive in terms of normal rainfall for the 2025 monsoon.

items.statement: New non-selective herbicide LAAFA addresses portfolio gap; ambition to make it a million-liter product.
items.quote: Our ambition would be that, you know, given our brand strength, can we make a kind of a million-liter kind of product?

items.statement: Worst case scenario: China starts dumping at cheaper price in India.
items.quote: Worst case scenario, China starts dumping at a cheaper price in India, but I guess , is there a possibility? The answer is yes.

items.statement: Seed business will continue to improve from current levels.
items.quote: I believe the seed will continue to improve from where we are.

items.statement: Soil and plant health business will also continue to improve.
items.quote: Our soil and plant health business will also continue to improve.

items.statement: Adding new portfolio in herbicide should improve.
items.quote: We are adding a new portfolio in herbicide. That should improve.

items.statement: Domestic prices in some pockets down 5% year-on-year; cost drop passed to consumer.
items.quote: And what we are talking about 5% is versus previous year, within which as well, our soil and plant health has seen good price traction.

items.statement: CSM business impacted due to customer scheduling; long-term prospects positive with new relationships.
items.quote: CSM business was impacted due to customer scheduling. However, long-term prospects are positive with work on new relationships .

items.statement: Export demand has seen recovery; carefully calibrating approach amid US tariffs.
items.quote: agrochemical export demand has seen a recovery . We are carefully calibrating our approach and amid ongoing U.S. tariffs and bilateral negotiations , w e will try to improve both volume growth and margin in a tough environment.

items.statement: North cotton hybrid continues good momentum with more than a million packets sold.
items.quote: North cotton hybrid continues to see good momentum with more than a million packet already sold.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments may cause short-term disruption in export market.
items.quote: Geopolitical developments may cause some disruption in the short term in the export market.

items.statement: Healthy cash and liquid fund balance of 439 crore as of 31st March 2025.
items.quote: As of 31st March ‘25, we are pleased to report a healthy cash and liquid fund balance of 439 crore and will further work to improve capital efficiency.

items.statement: Volumes lower sequentially and year-on-year due to challenging market environment and muted consumer sentiment; urban demand yet to pick up.
items.quote: As we have witnessed very challenging and volatile market environment, along with the muted consumer sentiments and urban demand yet to pick up in India. What we have seen is that our quarter 1 volumes are lower than quarter 1 -- sequential quarter as well as year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved significantly QoQ driven by better sales mix and efficiency measures despite lower volumes.
items.quote: However, the margins have been improved considerably on quarter-on-quarter, riding on the better sales mix, which is basically the discussions what we had in previous calls.

items.statement: EBITDA increased 55% QoQ to INR49.7 crore from INR32 crore in December 2024 quarter despite flat top line and lower volumes.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stands at INR49.7 crores, relatively flat at INR49.4 crores of March 2024 quarter. However, this represents an increase -- significant increase of 55% comparing to December 2024 quarter. December 2024, we had roughly INR32 crores of EBITDA.

items.statement: Strategic shift toward more profitable portfolio mix covering customers and products; sustainable (blueloop) products at 27-31% of sales.
items.quote: we talk about sustainable product sales, we've always maintain that. In the last few quarters, we are into the range of somewhere between 27% to 30%, 31% is the party our mix impact

items.statement: Efficiency measures across procurement, operations, and operating expenses under world-class operations program driving cost control.
items.quote: We are examining each and every aspect of our operations, I mean, end-to-end operations, not only employee. So overall, there is projects which are going through our -- we call it world-class operations umbrella. We focus on the overall productivity across the organization.

items.statement: Export sales typically 30% of revenue (70-30 domestic-export split); expected to maintain this ratio.
items.quote: When we look at the general split between our domestic sales and export sales, typically, we are into the range of 70-30 or kind of one-third, two-third kind of ratio we have. And we don't see any risk or we don't see any challenge, and we feel that we'll continue to maintain our ratios into that range.

items.statement: Capacity available to increase output; utilization not quantified due to product mix dependency.
items.quote: I think we do have capacity, Sukhbir, and there is room that we can do more, and we are continuously working on that. But it's very difficult to comment exactly on what percentage because it depends on product mix as well.

items.statement: Only borrowing is INR100 crore ECB; debt-equity 0.1, debt-to-EBITDA 2.1 (down from 3.2); strong liquidity with unutilized credit lines.
items.quote: Liquidity position is in good shape with the only borrowing on the books being the ECB of INR100 crores from this good company. Debt-equity ratio is very healthy at 0.1, in line with what we have in December '24 quarter and debt-to-EBITDA ratio at March at 2.1 compared to 3.2 end of December quarter.

items.statement: Working capital flat vs Q1 2024 but lagging behind December 2024 quarter.
items.quote: Working capital relatively flat when we compare with Q1 2024 at an overall level, though even lagging behind when we compare with the December '24 quarter.

items.statement: Servicing MNC customers like Unilever is extremely challenging due to their cost pressures flowing down.
items.quote: I think I have only one word to answer your -- this is exactly what's the challenge, it's extremely challenging at this moment. Because as yourself articulated that our end customers are also having challenges in their own business areas, and that puts pressure on cost at every level.

items.statement: Competitive landscape changed significantly over 5-7 years with more capacity in market; not comparable to pure-play film manufacturers.
items.quote: When you look at the competitive landscape, there's a big change in that. When we talk about companies, there are a lot of capacity in the market and all.

items.statement: Revenue flat at INR593 crore vs March 2024; down ~1% vs December 2024 quarter.
items.quote: The top line for the quarter stands at INR593 crores, which is almost flat when we look at March '24 quarter. However, slightly lower than December quarter by close to 1%.

items.statement: Significant improvement in safety metrics achieved this quarter.
items.quote: I'm pleased to say that we have achieved a significant improvement in our safety metrics this quarter. This progress reflects our dedication to fostering a secure work environment and reinforces our commitment to prioritizing employee well-being alongside business growth.

items.statement: Government regulations on plastic recycling and recyclable packaging evolving; expected to benefit sustainable product portfolio long-term.
items.quote: And apparently government, not only in India, but elsewhere also across the globe are taking measures to make the products recyclable and specifically packaging. And that definitely shall give us a great, I would say, benefit going forward.

items.statement: Urban demand recovery uncertain; consumption growth weak (1-2% volume growth in sector); adaptation of sustainable products slower due to ecosystem development.
items.quote: we were not so great. You have seen that rural is doing significantly better than the urban demand and all, but overall consumption scenario is not great. We have seen some results came in last 2 or 3 days, we are talking about the volume growth of 1% or 2% are not so

items.statement: No specific margin or volume targets given; focus on profitable core growth, sustainable products, operational efficiency, and digital transformation.
items.quote: Our strategy is to grow the profitable core. And we'll continue to look for opportunities which make sense for us, which will help us to improve both top line and bottom line. And I think that's a clear strength we had across so many quarters, and we'll continue to work on that.

items.statement: Guided 15% AUM growth for FY26 with better credit quality
items.quote: And overall for the next financial year, we expect to grow as the guidance given of 15% with better credit quality.

items.statement: Guided CV portfolio growth of 12-15% for FY26
items.quote: We are looking at 12% to 15% growth in the next financial year.

items.statement: Guided MSME portfolio growth of 18-20% for FY26
items.quote: I think our guidance on MSME would be between 18%-20% of growth for the financial year.

items.statement: Guided passenger vehicle portfolio growth of 20% for FY26
items.quote: Passenger vehicle, we are growing at 20% and we are confident of growing at 20%.

items.statement: Guided NIM of 8.5-8.6% for FY26
items.quote: We are guiding for an 8.45, 8.5, 8.6 kind of a NIM. Again, obviously if I get a rate benefit, some of it I would like to pass it on to my customer also. We would like to peg our NIM at about 8.6.

items.statement: Guided credit cost to be maintained around 2% and brought below 2%
items.quote: We always give a guidance that we will try to maintain around 2% and hopefully we should be able to bring it below 2% of credit cost.

items.statement: Guided cost-to-income ratio to improve to 27-28% over one year
items.quote: Yes, it should be hovering around between 27% to 28%.

items.statement: Guided 15-20 bps reduction in cost of funds for FY26
items.quote: So I will say around overall for the year, we will target close to around 15 to 20 basis point benefit in the cost.

items.statement: NIM declined to 8.25% in Q4 FY25 due to excess liquidity
items.quote: Our net interest margin was 8.25% as against 9.02% in Q4 FY'24 and 8.48% in Q3 FY'25. The decline in the NIM is mainly attributed to the excess liquidity maintained on the balance sheet, which will get re ctified in the coming quarters

items.quote: The current quarter will be around 20, 25 basis points.

items.quote: Our AUM has registered a growth of 17.05% over Q4 FY '24 and of 3.43 % sequentially. Our AUM stood at Rs. 263,190.27 crores as against Rs. 224,861.98 crores a year ago and Rs. 254,469.69 crores in Q3 FY '25.

items.quote: We have registered disbursement growth of 14.04% year -on-year. Our disbursements for the quarter aggregated to Rs. 44,847.93 crores versus Rs. 39,326.86 crores in Q4 FY24.

items.quote: Our asset quality, gross Stage-3 in Q4 FY '25 stood at 4.55% and net Stage-3 at 2.64% as against 5.45% gross and 2.7% net in Q4 FY '24 and 5.38% gross and 2.68% net in Q3 FY '25. items.quote: The written-off amount amounting to Rs. 2345 crores was already provided in the books of account and even after this write-off, there is no impact on the P&L per se.

items.quote: See, basically we had a provisioning cover of around 51% that has come down to 43 because of the numerator impact. items.quote: For the December quarter , it was 8.92 and for the March quarter it is 8.86. So that will translate into some cost reduction.

items.statement: Excess liquidity of Rs 31,000 crore (6 months of liabilities) expected to normalize to 3 months over next 2 quarters
items.quote: We always guide around 3 months of liability repayment to be in our liquid assets, but it is now close to around 6 months. We do expect this will come down in next 2 quarters to the earlier level of 3 months of liability repayment.

items.quote: The Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of Rs. 3 per equity share of nominal face value of 2, each fully paid up 150% for the Financial Year 2 024-'25. With this , total dividend for the Financial Year 2024-25 will be 9.9 per share of 2 each after adjusting for the split.

items.statement: Rural economy expected to support credit demand and quality with above-normal monsoon forecast
items.quote: This augurs well for us going forward also because the IMD prediction and Skymet prediction for the monsoon have been above average for this in the crop year and hopefully that will help the credit demand from the rural area to go up further and also help us in the credit quality.

items.statement: Government infrastructure spend revival expected to boost urban credit demand
items.quote: Hopefully , we should see revival in government spend on the infrastructure activities.

AI levers continue to help create proactive deals, maintain competitiveness, especially on Run-the-Business spend and underscore our differentiation through the use of our platform -led approach.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue $430 million, up 2.9% QoQ and 5.4% YoY in constant currency; highest sequential growth in 3 years
items.quote: Our Q4 FY25 revenue came in at $430 million, a growth of 2.9% sequentially and 5.4% YoY in constant currency terms. items.statement: EBIT margin stable at 15.3% in Q4 FY25; operating profit grew 3.9% QoQ and 11.7% YoY
items.quote: Looking at quarterly financial metrics, we delivered to our philosophy of maintaining margin in the stated band while making investments for growth. items.statement: EPS INR 23.5 in Q4 FY25, highest ever quarterly EPS, up 4.1% QoQ and 12.9% YoY
items.quote: EPS for the quarter was INR 23.5, the highest ever EPS in a single quarter and 4.1% sequential and a 12.9% YoY growth.

items.statement: Operating cash flow $52 million in Q4 FY25, 100% of net income; DSO 75 days, up 3 days QoQ
items.quote: Operating cash flow generation continues to be strong at USD 52 million for the quarter ; 100% of the net income. DSO of 75 days increased 3 days over the last quarter.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR 57 per share for full year FY25
items.quote: To this effect, the board of directors has also recommended a dividend of INR 57 per share for the full year FY25.

items.statement: Client pyramid improved YoY: added 1 client in $75M+ band, 1 in $20M+, 3 in $5M+; top 10 accounts grew 5.8% QoQ
items.quote: Our client pyramid continues to improve across the board. A couple of new accounts we signed recently have already grown to over $60 million on a quarterly annualized basis.

items.quote: So, one demand is okay in the car segment. It is okay in the 2-wh eeler segment. The problem seems to be in the commercial vehicle segment

name: SBI Cards and Payment Services Ltd

items.statement: Expect cost of funds to gradually decline in FY26 benefiting from RBI rate action; NIM expected to be steady with upward bias
items.quote: We expect cost of fund to be on a gradual downward trend in financial year '25-'26, benefiting from the RBI rate action and expect the NIM to be steady.

items.statement: Expect receivables growth of 12-14% in FY26

items.statement: Expect cost-to-income ratio of 55-57% for FY26

items.statement: Confident aerospace momentum will carry forward into FY26
items.quote: We are confident that this momentum will be carried forward into FY26.
